findings.issue: The nested Vitest inherits FORCE_COLOR (and similar color vars) from the parent environment through sandboxEnv(). When color is forced, Vitest wraps the summary counts in ANSI codes, so /Tests\s+2 passed/ and /Tests\s+2 failed/ no longer match and both acceptance tests fail even though the behaviour is correct. This is a false failure that depends on the environment, in a test meant to remove CI flakiness. GitHub Actions does not set FORCE_COLOR by default, so CI passes today. But any developer shell or tool that exports FORCE_COLOR breaks local `npm test`.
findings.evidence: `FORCE_COLOR=1 npx vitest run tests/ci/speed-limits.acceptance.test.ts` -> 2 failed: "AssertionError: expected '\n\u001b[1m\u001b[30m\u001b[46m RUN \u2026' to match /Tests\s+2 passed/" and the same for /Tests\s+2 failed/. Without FORCE_COLOR, both pass (2.7 s each).
findings.fix: In runPerfSuites, after building env, add `delete env.FORCE_COLOR; env.NO_COLOR = '1';`, or strip ANSI escapes from the output before matching. The file is listed in state.json locked_tests, so the orchestrator must unlock it first.

summary: The change matches the spec. speedLimitsEnforced is exactly env.CI !== 'true'. With CI=true, only the rate/build asserts and the p95 failure collection are gated. The checksum asserts, the per-scenario method asserts and the bounded-work error-message asserts still always run. Without CI, the threshold env names/defaults (1e6, 500, 20) and the 2000 ms ceiling are unchanged, and the full-speed commands in the README and headers are verbatim. sandboxEnv is exported, not copied, and scrubs VITEST*/NODE_V8_COVERAGE/TEST*. The nested run uses `npx vitest run`, so there is no --coverage and vite.config has no coverage.enabled. CI is deleted for the local case. No locked file, src/** or .github file was touched. The acceptance tests fail if either gate is inverted or removed in either suite. Verified locally: the new tests pass, and `CI=true ... -t "bounds the work"` passes with 1 test. One MAJOR: the acceptance test's summary regex fails when FORCE_COLOR is inherited. SPEC-04/06 mutation probes were not run: they edit src, and this review is read-only.
